title: Assigning Distinct Integers
statementMd:
You are given $n$ positive integers $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$.

Construct a sequence of $n$ pairwise distinct positive integers $b_1,b_2,\dots,b_n$ such that $b_i\ge a_i$ for every $1\le i\le n$. First, minimize $\sum_{i=1}^{n}b_i$. Among all sequences with the minimum sum, output the lexicographically smallest one.

A sequence $(x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n)$ is lexicographically smaller than $(y_1,y_2,\dots,y_n)$ if there is an index $p$ such that $x_i=y_i$ for every $1\le i \lt p$, and $x_p \lt y_p$.

## Input

The first line contains an integer $T$ ($1\le T\le 10^4$), the number of test cases.

For each test case:

- The first line contains an integer $n$ ($1\le n\le 3\times 10^5$).
- The second line contains $n$ integers $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$ ($1\le a_i\le 10^9$).

It is guaranteed that the sum of $n$ over all test cases does not exceed $3\times 10^5$.

## Output

For each test case, output one line containing $n$ integers $b_1,b_2,\dots,b_n$, separated by single spaces.

## Note

In the first test case, the minimum possible sum is $1+2+3=6$.

In the third test case, every optimal sequence uses the values $1,2,3$. The lexicographically smallest valid order is $(2,1,3)$.
